literal: Being begged of is painful, until the moment of seeing the pleasant face of those who begged.
translation: Being begged for alms is painful, but only until one sees the joyful, pleasant face of those who receive the gift.
modern: பிறர் நம்மிடம் வந்து இரந்து கேட்பது துன்பமானதுதான்; ஆனால், இரந்து கேட்டவரின் மகிழ்ச்சியான முகத்தைக் காணும் வரை மட்டுமே அத்துன்பம் நீடிக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet explores the psychological experience of giving charity. The act of being asked for help (irakka-patutal) can initially feel unpleasant or painful (innatu) to a giver, perhaps due to the burden of giving or witnessing another's distress. However, this discomfort lasts only until (alavu) the giver beholds the sweet, joyful face (inmukam) of the recipient upon receiving the aid. The sight of the beggar's happiness instantly transforms the giver's pain into profound joy, highlighting the ultimate reward of charity.
